beats.text: You saw a rescue. But Jean Grey freed Logan from Apocalypse by erasing his past, and Marvel's Wolverine told you the cost before she did it.
beats.tts: You saw a rescue. But Jean Grey freed Logan from Apocalypse by erasing his past, and Marvel's Wolverine told you the cost before she did it.

beats.text: It is easy to read the ending as a sad rescue. Logan survives and walks away with a clean slate. This video argues the other side. The ending is an erasure, and the game sets it up long before the final fight. So did Jean rescue Logan, or did she erase him? Fair warning: full spoilers for the whole game, including the post-credits scene.

beats.text: The answer comes down to one warning Jean gives and four words Logan says back. The four words sound kind. By the end of this video they'll sound like the saddest line in the game. Getting there takes a story Jean tells about the 1800s, and a villain who spent the whole game reaching into Logan's head too.

beats.text: Start with what the game wants you to believe. Logan, real name James Howlett, has holes in his memory, and the whole story is him trying to piece together who he is. About three years before it starts, he walked out on Team X, his old black-ops unit. Now the unit is back together, because the man who built it, Nathaniel Essex, has been captured. The old team blames Logan for leaving, Sabretooth loudest of all. Logan heals from almost anything. That matters, because the wound this ending leaves is one his healing factor can't touch.

beats.text: For most of the game Essex is the father figure, the man Logan and Victor Creed, Sabretooth, set out to save. The game shows you why early on, with a frightened wild man in a jungle and a calm voice offering him somewhere to belong.

beats.text: No one in the scene says the wild man's name, though the subtitles label him Logan. The voice gives its own name, Nathaniel Essex, then asks for his. So the game opens on a man who can't speak for himself while someone else tells him where he belongs. The final conversation has the same shape, with Jean doing the telling. Remember the word home. It comes back.

beats.chapter: She burned it out once before

beats.text: The game's lore ties that name to Apocalypse, the ancient mutant Logan once served as his Horseman of Death. Back then, Jean did something about it.

beats.cue: GAME AUDIO 109, 84-92.6 s: "I burnt every trace of Death out of your mind. Or so I thought." (subtitle wording; v6 adds 0.6 s so 'thought' finishes)

beats.text: Or so she thought. By her account, Logan chased her across the world for ages. She died a few times and was reborn into other lives, and somehow he kept finding her. When she came across a cabin he'd built, she ran to the only place she felt safe. She calls it home. She also admits she didn't know if he'd come to kiss her or kill her, and neither did he. Even in her oldest memory, the Death in Logan might hurt her. The finale asks that question again.

beats.text: That's my reading, and here's what it rests on: the first burn didn't hold, she talks about how many times she's done this with him, she plans for being separated again, and her fairy tale, which we'll get to, ends with "for a while". The game never draws the circle, but those pieces make a loop. A darkness settles on Logan, Jean burns it out, it comes back, and they find each other again. This time Jean keeps her memories and Logan loses his. If I'm right, this rescue doesn't end the story. It starts it over.

And he explains what he did to the Helix Engine.

beats.text: Put Essex next to Jean and the design gets clearer. Both of them reach into Logan's mind, and both show him a home. Essex builds a cabin out of what Logan wants. Jean, as you'll see, takes him to a garden made of what they had. Each of them also has a story about someone they loved who agreed to it. Essex took from his wife to make himself more. Jean is about to take from Logan and leave him less. The game makes the villain's version easy to condemn. Hers is much harder, and I think that's the point.

beats.text: There's one more reason this isn't a clean rescue. Apocalypse is never defeated. The Phoenix forces him out of Logan's mind, and that's all. Victor Creed fights beside Logan for most of the game, and only once, late, do they turn on each other. His reason is the word this whole game keeps coming back to: family. You destroyed our family, he tells Logan. He also used the Helix Engine on himself, and now he carries Apocalypse's voice too.
